events.title: Subversion 1.0 released
events.summary: CollabNet shipped Subversion 1.0 on February 23, 2004 — a centralized version control system designed to replace CVS.
events.about: Subversion (SVN) tracks file history with atomic commits, cheap branching, and real directory versioning — fixes CVS lacked. It powered thousands of corporate repos and open-source projects through the 2000s before Git won mindshare. Typical workflow: `svn checkout`, edit, `svn commit` to a central server.

narrative.whyChosen: SVN was the mainstream upgrade path from CVS for a decade of professional development.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved centralized VCS could be fixed without going fully distributed like Git.
narrative.problemSolved: CVS lacked atomic commits and reliable branching; teams needed a drop-in successor.
